contexts.text: By the daughters, whom he will take for spice-dealers, cooks, and bakers () are signified the good things of doctrine, by means of which he will delight those (principles of falsity), and will make them favourable.

The (sensual things) which are subordinate to the intellectual part are represented by the butler of the King of Egypt, and those which are subordinate to the voluntary part, by the baker. That the former are kept, but the latter cast out, is represented by the butler's returning to his post, and the baker's being hung. AC 5082. AC 5094.

The baker = those things in the body which are subject to the voluntary part. The baker = the outward Sensual, or the Sensual of the body, which is subordinate or subject to the voluntary part of the inward man. The reason a baker has this signification, is that everything which is of service for eating, or which is eaten, as bread, food in general, and all the work of the baker, is predicated of good, and thus relates to the voluntary part...
The butler and the baker (represent the Lord) as to those things which are of the outward Natural.

And the prince of the bakers saw = the perception of the Sensual subject to the voluntary part... The prince of the bakers = the Sensual subject to the voluntary part in general, thus those sensual things. AC 5232.
The work of the baker = according to the whole use of the Sensual... The baker = the Sensual subject to the voluntary part. AC 5163.
They are all adulterers, as an oven heated by the baker... (). An oven = the delight of cupidities, which are of evils.
Like bread from the baker in the mouth...

That they have perverted goods and truths by means of their own loves, is signified by their all being adulterers, as an oven heated by the baker. To commit adultery = to pervert good and thence truth; this is compared to an oven heated by the baker, because they put falsities together as it were into a lump which is favourable to their own loves... That hence come nothing but the evils of their loves, favoured by falsities, is signified by the baker sleeping the whole night, in the morning it burneth as a fire of flame, they are all hot like an oven (). They are compared to a baker, and an oven, because they put doctrine together from falsities, as a baker makes bread and pastry in an oven.

Since by a baker is signified the good of love, the same as by bread; and by a butler, the truth of doctrine, the same as by wine, the baker, for his offence against King Pharaoh, was hung. (That is, crucified; see AE 655:4).
